title: Harness history event
description: One row of the one history (epic #59): today's event envelope plus where the row came from (provenance). Every row from every era (main, dogfood, dogfood2, sessions, GitHub, the live runtime) has this shape. A field that could not be recovered holds a legacy placeholder, never an invented value, and provenance.placeholders lists its path. Rows are never edited: a format change adds an event version and a declared conversion. src/history.js reads this file; nothing restates it.

schemaVersion.description: The history schema the row was written in (schemaVersion above). A row without one was written before the field and is at absentMeans. A page that reads the history declares the range it reads (pages/<page>/needs.json, reads.schemaVersion) and, on a history with a row outside it, shows a red banner naming the mismatch and no data.

id.description: The event id as its source wrote it. Ids are unique within one source, not across sources (dogfood and dogfood2 share orchestrator ids).

version.description: The row's position in the one history, counted from 1 in time order.

to.description: The machine address the event went to (harness, budget, item:<id>, item:<id>/decision:<...>).

relayedBy.description: The session that relayed a tap or message (harness meta.sources).

harness.description: The harness that applied (or, for a recovered row, would have applied) the event.

route.description: The route the event took when it was written: the ids of the routes ("route" in the machine JSON) its transitions took, in order. Replay takes this route (harness meta.store.facts). A row written before routes were recorded has none.

v.description: The event type's version (events below). Absent means 1.

legacy.description: Why the value is missing, e.g. 'main predates the envelope (M1)'.
A placeholder for a value that could not be recovered.

actor.description: Who sent the event. The kinds and id forms are harness meta.actors.

source.description: Where the event came from. The kinds are harness meta.sources.

ref.description: A path under harness/archive/ (or the live store's name), as C1 lays it out.

line.description: The line (JSONL) or event index the row was read from.

origin.description: live: the runtime wrote it into this history (live below: such a row carries no provenance, and is read with this origin). migrated: copied from an older store, upcast. recovered: reconstructed from a session transcript, GitHub or the Library, where no store recorded it.

also.description: Other sources that described the same fact (identity below); the merger keeps them here.

placeholders.description: Paths in this row (actor, harness, event.sha, ...) that hold a legacy placeholder. Exactly those, no more and no fewer.

confidence.description: Only on a recovered row where reading the source took judgement; the from line points at the evidence.

events.description: Every event type the history holds, with its current version and the payload fields it needs to mean anything (a weak schema: the rest are optional, because eras differ). Every type the machines take is here; OUT_OF_BAND, which records work done outside the gates, the item takes as a fact; and ERA_ENDED, which ends a store's era, no machine takes: replay applies it itself (harness meta.store.eras). A version above 1 needs a declared conversion from each earlier one. Every field a page reads (pages/<page>/needs.json) is a property here, in the envelope or in its type's schema, so dropping one fails naming the page and the field.

CHECKS_PASSED.description: CI passed on one head of the PR. sha is the wake's short head sha. head, which harness from-github reads from GitHub's REST API (never from the wake) and harness verify-facts reads again, is the head fact a PASS carries to a merge of main by (workItem merging, #137): sha, the full head sha; parents, its parents; onMain, the one parent GitHub's compare says is reachable from the PR's base branch, or null; diff, for a merge with a parent on main, the diff hash against that parent of the head and of the other parent (src/github-read.js diffHash), each by its sha. Rows from before #137 have no head.

ERA_ENDED.description: The end of a store's era (harness meta.store.eras): era is the store's archive ref, snapshot its harness snapshot as its state.json holds it, and pending the effects its outbox holds that it never acked, each as the outbox holds it without its eventId and at (its id, which replay queues as sourceId, is the one the era's host knows it by; a mark written before #146 holds none). scripts/history/join.mjs --from writes one per store, after the store's last row (at: the later of that row's time and state.json's updatedAt), id era:<store>, provenance.from the store. No one sent it, so its actor and source are placeholders (upcast legacy.era), and its harness is the release state.json names as its writer (writtenBy), else a placeholder too. The rows before it keep their type and payload as their store wrote them; replay takes each item's state at the era's end from snapshot, never by re-judging those rows.

PERSON_DECIDED.description: A tap on a decision card. choice is the decision's own word (decision context.options: approve, revise, reject); a session's record of the tap (scripts/history/extract-session.mjs) also keeps label, the option the card showed, and where that label is no decision card's (src/card.js), choice is a legacy placeholder.

OUT_OF_BAND.description: Work done outside the gates on someone's order (a merge by hand on the person's say-so, #46 and #52). It is history, never a reason for a new store: who ordered it, the message that did, what was done, which gates or states were skipped and the PR it touched (pr). A landing also names the head that landed (sha). A session sends it to the item with harness send, in any state of the item, done and cancelled included: the item takes it as a fact (workItem on.OUT_OF_BAND, harness meta.store records), its state unchanged. harness doctor lists every one, and does not count a landing one records as a problem (harness meta.invariants reviewOnHead). An order given by no chat message (a button pressed on GitHub) holds a legacy placeholder in message.

live.description: A row the runtime wrote into this history (harness meta.store.history). runtime.apply writes the same envelope in every store and no provenance, so a store that is not a history stays as it was and a row is never rewritten to carry one. In a history, a row with no provenance after the last row that has one is live: the join writes provenance on every row of the new store it makes and never adds to one, so its rows end there and only the runtime appends after them. Its provenance is the one below, {store} the history's own name (its folder, as a store is state/<name>). src/history.js historyRows applies it, the one place that does, and harness doctor holds every row of a history to this schema as historyRows gives it. A row with no provenance before the last row that has one is not live, and stays a problem (provenance: missing).

upcast.description: How E1 (scripts/history/extract-store.mjs) migrates a row from a store that predates a field, as main predates the event envelope: each envelope field listed here, and each field its event type needs (events.types required), that the row does not hold becomes a legacy placeholder, its text the template for its kind ({store}: the archive ref the store was read as; {field}: the path; {type}: the event type), and provenance.placeholders lists it. Nothing else is filled in, and nothing is guessed from other fields (an id that names a PR is not its pr): a row that still fails validate is skipped with why.

legacy.event: {store} recorded no {field} on its {type} rows then
legacy.era: {store}'s era ends here: no one sent this row, it carries {store}'s state.json

identity.description: How the merger knows two rows describe one fact (C4). The first rule whose types include the row's type gives its key: the values at the listed paths, joined. A key path the rule abbreviates (abbrev: path to n) is compared on its first n characters, as git abbreviates a commit, so a short sha and the full one are one key. A row missing any key path keeps a key of its own and is never merged. Of rows with one key, the row is kept whose provenance.from.source is the rule's first owner (its owners in order) that has one, else the earliest, and the others' from go to its provenance.also. Rows with one key that disagree on a payload field both have (a key path agrees by its key) are a conflict the merger reports, never merges silently. Two rows of one source (provenance.from.ref) are never one fact: a source records a fact once, so the second row of a key in one source is that key's second fact (a stand-in's answer and its re-ask under a grant share a decision address), and the n-th of one source is one fact only with the n-th of another, in time order. Nor are two rows of two stores: each store is its own era (harness meta.store.eras), so the stores count as one source here, and an item filed again in a later store is filed twice, once in each era.

rules.why: A PR merges once. The store's row is kept where it has one: it carries the actor, release and route replay applies. Else GitHub's (scripts/history/extract-github.mjs) is kept: it binds the PR to its item and names the head that landed, and a session's merge call (scripts/history/extract-session.mjs) names no item. The others go to also.
CI on one head of one PR. The store names the head by the wake's short sha and GitHub by the full one; the store's row is kept where it has one, GitHub's goes to also.
An item id is filed once.
A card is one message: its id names it in every source. A session's request_decision call (scripts/history/extract-session.mjs) names no decision address, so the address cannot key it.
The person decides only by a tap on a card (harness meta.actors person), so a tap is named by the card it answers, its source ref, in the store and in the session the tap reached alike.
The decision address is item + class + attempt; the store owns machine decisions.
One Agent tool call is one spawn.
The order is a message the session read.

otherwise.why: Any other row is its own fact within its source.

steps.description: What each row of a history did, beside it in steps.jsonl: one step per row, in the history's order, joined to its row by version (and id). harness replay --steps writes it by replaying the history with the current code, each row a fact (harness meta.store.facts), and reads it off its scratch copy before and after each row: the actors whose state the row changed, the context fields it changed, the effects it queued with the acks the store holds for them, and its route. A row replay cannot apply is a step with the reason (refused) and no changes, and a row of an era a later ERA_ENDED row ends is a step naming that era (era) and no changes. A page that reads it (pages/<page>/needs.json reads.with) declares the fields it reads here, so dropping one fails naming the page and the field.

version.description: The history row this step is.

era.description: The era the row is a fact of (harness meta.store.eras), whose ERA_ENDED row holds what it did: replay did not apply it, so it changed nothing and queued nothing here. null for a row replay applied with today's machine, an ERA_ENDED row included.

refused.description: Why replay could not apply the row (a second row of an id it applied already is one: replay applies an id once); null when it applied it.

route.description: The ids of the routes the row took on replay; null when it was refused.

actors.description: Each actor whose state the row changed: its address (harness, item:<id>, item:<id>/<child id>) and its state before and after, as text (null: the actor was not there).

context.description: Each context field the row changed: the actor's address, the field, and its value before and after (null: absent).

effects.description: Each effect the row queued (id, name, subject, and its detail as the outbox holds it, null when it has none) and the acks the store holds for it, oldest first (none: pending, or a store that keeps no acks, as a history joined without its stores' acks).

usage.description: Time and tokens by item, beside a history in usage.jsonl. scripts/history/usage.mjs writes it from the session ledgers the Stop hook files (ledger/sessions/<session>.json: each turn with its own usage and the subagents it started), the agent records beside them (<session>/agents/<agentId>.json: bind.item, bind.spawn and resumes; <session>/calls/: each call the hook recorded) and a store's or a history's rows. A segment row is one start of an agent: its first start and each resume its record lists. The agent (session/agentId, one run) is tied to an item by its record's bind.item, else by the WORKER_STARTED row that names it; its role is that of the WORKER_SPAWNED row whose toolUseId is bind.spawn; its agentType and model are the ledger's. The first segment starts at the WORKER_STARTED time (else at the start of the turn that lists the agent) and a resume at its time; the last segment ends at the first start plus the ledger's durationMs, and a segment before a resume ends at the agent's last call the hook recorded before that resume, a lower bound. The ledger counts an agent's whole transcript, so its counts are on the last segment and an earlier segment's are placeholders: summed over the segments they are counted once. An agent the ledger lists more than once is its transcript filed again: its counts are the listing with the most requests (the latest of equals), never a sum. A lead row is a turn of a session that wrote rows for an item (rows whose actor is that session, sent to the item or REQUEST_RECEIVED for it, inside the turn's start..end), with the turn's own usage (not its subagents'), once, naming every item it wrote for. A value no ledger holds is a legacy placeholder, never a guess. A subagent tied to no item has no segment row: the session row of its ledger names it with the reason and its cost, and usage.mjs also reports it on stderr. Each session ledger read is one session row, so a session the history names with no session row has no ledger. A page that reads this file (pages/<page>/needs.json reads.onDemand, or reads.with to read it with the history at render and on refresh) declares the fields it reads here, so dropping one fails naming the page and the field.

anyOf.description: One start of an agent, until it stopped.
A turn of the lead that wrote rows for these items, with its own usage.
A session ledger usage.mjs read, once, with each subagent it lists that no item could be tied to (the agent's session/agentId, its agentType, why it is tied to none, and its cost at list price).
